response.title: Corn stover to ethanol, the NREL 2011 design
response.description: The corn stover ethanol biorefinery the BioSTEAM authors built to the NREL design report (Humbird et al. 2011, NREL/TP-5100-47764): pretreatment, enzymatic hydrolysis, co-fermentation, distillation, wastewater treatment and a boiler, run whole on the package's own defaults. The benchmark: it shows this installation simulates and prices a published biorefinery as its authors do.
response.priceBasis: USD per gallon of ethanol, at the package's own ethanol density

response.title: Dry-grind corn to ethanol, the conventional plant
response.description: The conventional dry-grind corn ethanol plant the BioSTEAM authors built after Kwiatkowski et al. 2006 (Industrial Crops and Products): milling and slurry, jet cooking and liquefaction, saccharification, simultaneous saccharification and fermentation by yeast, the ethanol purification train of biorefineries.ethanol (beer column, rectifier, molecular sieves), and DDGS and crude corn oil recovered from the stillage. Run whole on the package's own defaults: the yeast program's reference biorefinery, with the package's own regression values beside what this installation computes.

response.title: Glucose to ethanol, draft v0
response.description: A glucose solution into a batch fermenter, then the ethanol purification train of the BioSTEAM reference designs (beer column, rectifier, molecular sieves), giving fuel-grade ethanol. The fermenter turns glucose into ethanol at the bound yield as a share of the theoretical yield, for a batch time of titre over productivity. Chemicals and finance are the dry-grind corn ethanol plant's; equipment and thermodynamics are BioSTEAM's own; no number is the flowsheet's.

inputs.name: glucose in the fermenter's feed
inputs.note: records of a medium component whose carbon source is glucose; sets the water that dilutes the glucose, by thermosteam's volume of the solution

inputs.name: ethanol titre at harvest
inputs.note: with the productivity, sets the batch time; the beer's own ethanol follows from the feed's glucose and the yield, and the run reads it back

inputs.name: ethanol yield on glucose
inputs.note: the fermenter's conversion is this yield over the theoretical yield of the reaction; a case above the theoretical yield cannot run, and says so

inputs.name: ethanol volumetric productivity
inputs.note: the batch time is the titre divided by it

inputs.name: ethanol fermented in a year
inputs.note: a named person's assumption; with the yield it sets the glucose fed, so the plant's size

inputs.name: price of glucose
inputs.note: a named person's assumption; the glucose alone is priced, not its water

inputs.name: ethanol purity
inputs.note: fuel grade: the ethanol the package's molecular sieves give, with no denaturant blended; a convention every run's basis names, and the run reads the purity back

response.priceBasis: USD per kg of fuel-grade ethanol, as the product leaves its tank
leavesOut: where the glucose comes from: it arrives as clean glucose, priced as such
cell mass and by-products: the glucose the yield does not turn into ethanol leaves unconverted in the stillage
the scrubber that recovers ethanol from the fermenter's gas

response.title: A vessel and a train, priced
response.description: A glucose solution into the fermenter fermOS designed (a kept fermos.vessel design: BioSTEAM's AeratedBioreactor or NREL batch fermenter, rebuilt as the same class with every design parameter as the design holds it, running the reaction the design was built on), its beer through the units of a train pureOS ran (a kept pureos.train_run: each unit the same catalogue type, class and values as that run held them), priced with the dry-grind corn ethanol plant's TEA (biorefineries.corn.create_tea, ConventionalEthanolTEA), its financial parameters in the panel's Finance group as the package's defaults until a person sets one. A scenario on it names the vessel design and the train run. The train's own inlet is not an input: the fermenter's beer is its inlet. Only the yeast program has a chemical set, so a vessel or a train of another program is refused.

inputs.name: glucose in the fermenter's feed
inputs.note: records of a medium component whose carbon source is glucose; sets the water that dilutes the glucose, by thermosteam's volume of the solution

inputs.name: ethanol titre at harvest
inputs.note: with the productivity, sets the fermenter's batch time; the reacting time the vessel was designed for is named beside it in the run's basis

inputs.name: ethanol yield on glucose
inputs.note: sets the conversion of the vessel's reaction: the yield over the ethanol that reaction makes of a gram of glucose; a case above it cannot run, and says so

inputs.name: ethanol volumetric productivity
inputs.note: the batch time is the titre divided by it

inputs.name: ethanol fermented in a year
inputs.note: the vessel's scale: the plant scale its design names (the vessel design is its source); a design of one vessel's batch volume names none, and then it is a named person's assumption. With the yield it sets the glucose fed, so the plant's size

inputs.name: price of glucose
inputs.note: a named person's assumption; the glucose alone is priced, not its water

response.priceBasis: USD per kg of the product the train traces (ethanol, for the yeast program), contained in the train's product stream as it leaves the train's last unit
leavesOut: where the glucose comes from: it arrives as clean glucose, priced as such
every outlet the train does not send on leaves the plant unpriced: no co-product credit and no waste treatment
by-products the vessel's reaction does not make, and the scrubber that would recover product from the fermenter's gas
